title: Kinetic Energy Transfer Simulation
description: A rigged humanoid figure stands on a platform and kicks a ShaderBall, transferring kinetic energy based on user-configured parameters. The user adjusts leg swing force, friction, gravity, and ball mass, then triggers the kick to watch the ShaderBall roll, bounce, and decelerate across a physics-simulated ground plane with real-time energy readouts.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a kinetic energy transfer simulation. Load RiggedFigure.glb and ShaderBall.glb using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: a large flat ground plane with grid texture, soft ambient light (0x404060), a directional light casting shadows, and a perspective camera at position (4, 3, 6) looking at the origin. Use OrbitControls for camera manipulation. Place the RiggedFigure at (-2, 0, 0) facing right, and the ShaderBall at (0.5, 0.4, 0) scaled to radius ~0.4. Build a GUI panel (HTML/CSS overlay, no dat.gui) with these controls: (1) a 'Kick Force' slider (range 1-20, default 8), (2) a 'Ball Mass' slider (range 0.5-10 kg, default 2), (3) a 'Ground Friction' slider (range 0.01-0.5, default 0.15), (4) a 'Gravity' slider (range 1-20 m/s², default 9.8), (5) a 'Spin Factor' slider (range 0-1, default 0.3), and (6) a 'Launch Angle' slider (range 0-45 degrees, default 10). Add a 'KICK' button that triggers the simulation. When kicked: animate the RiggedFigure's right leg bones (find leg bones in the skeleton hierarchy) in a forward swing motion over 0.4 seconds, then apply velocity to the ShaderBall computed as force/mass at the launch angle. Simulate ball physics each frame: apply gravity to vertical velocity, detect ground collision with coefficient of restitution 0.5, apply friction to horizontal velocity, and rotate the ball proportional to horizontal speed times spin factor. Display a real-time HUD showing current kinetic energy (0.5*m*v²), velocity magnitude, and distance traveled. Add a 'RESET' button to return everything to initial state. The ball should leave a fading trail (use a line or particle trail). Validate that all parameter changes reflect in the simulation output. Ensure shadows are enabled on renderer, ground, and all meshes.
